name: aversion
quote: That painting is ugly as sin.
description: Unattractiveness to the senses or sensibilities in purely subjective arena.
perceptions: Something brings dismay by being judged as a poorly-formed instance of its type of thing.
results: preference to not experience this often

variations.name: aversion for a particular outcome
variations.description: The sensation of not wanting a particular thing to happen while being aware it might happen.
examples: Not wanting your kid to get hurt in the competition.
Not wanting to find a spider under your bed.

comparisons.description: Disgust is the perception that the target could somehow contaminate you. Aversion is simply not liking the thing without perceiving that it could somehow taint you.
You 'hate' things that you never want to experience again. Aversion is weaker - you find the thing 'poorly-formed' but can probably tolerate experiencing it again.

You can have an aversion to a specific trait or thing without necessarily disrespecting the person as whole. For instance, you may be averse to your mother smoking, but not that may not be enough to make you disrespect her.

You can have an aversion to a specific trait or thing without necessarily feeling superior to the person showing it. Contempt involves a more fundamental judgment about the other person's inherent worth or capabilities, leading to a sense of superiority.

You can have an aversion to something or someone without necessarily having a sense of 'ill will'. You may just want the punk rocker to change their greasy hair style while not wishing them negativity.

variations.name: aesthetic aversion
variations.description: Something unattractive to the senses or sensibilities in art or music.
perceptions: An artistic representation of something brings dismay by being considered poorly-formed for that kind of thing.
examples: music from a genre you don't favor

variations.name: physical aversion
variations.description: A particularly unattractive item, ideal, or person may create a desire to avoid it/him/her.
perceptions: A person or item is judged to be poorly-formed.

variations.name: aversion signaling
variations.description: Unattractiveness to the senses or sensibilities driven at least in part by a recognition that a social group expects us to find a certain thing unappealing.
perceptions: A social group will want me to dislike this thing.
The thing disappoints because it is poorly-formed.

guidance.description: If desired, there are various resources available for how to gently resist social pressure.

commentaries.quote: The factors that you use to determine whether something is unattractive (poorly-formed) depend on culture and individual experience.
Aesthetic aversion is always subjective. Someone else may appreciate the architecture, singing voice, graffiti, or clashing colors.
A feeling of aversion or attachment toward something is your clue that there's work to be done.
